# Tesla recalls 20,349 vehicles because headlights may reduce visibility for other drivers

Tesla recall 

A problem with headlight brightness has led Tesla to recall 20,349 vehicles, according to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration. Documents posted by the agency say the recall impacts certain 2017-2023 Model 3 and 2020-2023 Model Y vehicles.
results.title: Tesla recalls 20,349 vehicles because headlights may reduce visibility for other drivers

results.content:
Tesla, Inc. issued a recall for 20,349 Model 3 and Model Y vehicles because the headlight low beams may be too bright, exceeding the maximum light output, according to a National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) recall report.

As of Aug. 2, Tesla was aware of three warranty claims and one field report related to the issue. No crashes, injuries or deaths had been reported to the vehicle manufacturer. [...] As of Aug. 4, Tesla had not identified a remedy for the headlight issue. Vehicle owners may contact Tesla customer service at 1-877-798-3752. Tesla's recall number is SB-24-17-003.

Greta Cross is a national trending reporter at USA TODAY. Story idea? Email her atgcross@usatod

results.content:
Tesla has issued a recall on over 20,349 Model 3 and Model Y vehicles which have low-beam headlights that exceed the maximum brightness. Unlike many Tesla recalls, this one seems like it will require a physical fix, rather than a software update.

The recall covers 18,735 Model Y vehicles from 2020-2023 and 1,614 Model 3s from 2017-2023. Affected vehicles have headlamp assembly 1077371-98-L and 1077372-00-L, supplied by Marelli Automotive Lighting. [...] Tesla has been subject to many recalls over its days, but oftentimes it’s a bit of a non-story, because the NHTSA lumps all recalls into the same system, including ones that can be fixed by software updates.
